case_name: Manager, R.B.I., Bangalore v S. Mani and Others
facts: The Respondents herein were Ticca Mazdoors working under the Appellant herein.
Ticca Mazdoors are intermittently appointed by the Reserve Bank of India whenever absence of regular Class IV employees takes place.
They are not engaged everyday or continuously.
Their engagement depends upon the need of the Appellant.
They are never regarded as regular Mazdoors.
Two waiting lists are maintained by the Appellant.
The first waiting list contains the names of such of them who may be appointed as regular Mazdoors whereas the second list is maintained for those who are to be engaged as Ticca Mazdoors.
The name of the respondents figured in the second list.
They were appointed in the said category as Ticca Mazdoor between the period 14th March, 1980 and 8th August, 1982 for the purpose of their appointment as regular Mazdoors.
issues: Whether the Respondents' terminations were illegal
Whether the Respondents are entitled to be reinstated in service with full back wages
petitioner_arguments: The Appellant did not prove its case that the Respondents had abandoned their services.
The Tribunal misdirected itself in passing the impugned award insofar as it considered irrelevant factors and failed to take into consideration the relevant facts.
No adverse inference could have been drawn for non-production of attendance register as sufficient explanation therefor had been furnished.
The burden of proof in that behalf lay upon the Respondents
The judgments of the criminal court having been rendered by giving benefit of doubt to the Respondents herein, the same itself could not have been a ground for grant of relief.
respondent_arguments: The Respondents' contentions that they continued in service, from March 1980 to August 1982 as disclosed in their pleadings and representations, having not been denied, the same must be held to have been admitted.
As the Appellant herein could not prove its case that the Respondents had abandoned their services, the Tribunal rightly placed the onus of proof on it;

Although by reason of the Respondents' being reinstated in service, they would continue to have the status of Ticca Mazdoors, but having regard to the intervening circumstances, viz., the settlement arrived at by and between the Appellant and the Union, they would be entitled to be regularized in services

Section 25F of the Industrial Disputes Act being mandatory in nature, the provisions thereof are required to be complied with even when the workmen were employed as Badli Workers or Ticca Mazdoors as daily wager.
court_reasoning: The Tribunal rightly placed the onus of proof on the Appellant
The impugned award could have been passed upon drawing an adverse inference

The Respondents' contentions that they continued in service, from March 1980 to August 1982 as disclosed in their pleadings and representations, having not been denied, the same must be held to have been admitted.

Although by reason of the Respondents' being reinstated in service, they would continue to have the status of Ticca Mazdoors, but having regard to the intervening circumstances, viz., the settlement arrived at by and between the Appellant and the Union, they would be entitled to be regularized in services

Section 25F of the Industrial Disputes Act being mandatory in nature, the provisions thereof are required to be complied with even when the workmen were employed as Badli Workers or Ticca Mazdoors as daily wager.
holding: The Respondents having completed 240 days of service; and their terminations having been brought about without complying with the provisions of Section 25F of the Industrial Disputes Act, and, thus, being illegal they were entitled to be reinstated in the Bank's services as per the prevailing rules and conditions of the service with full back wages.
